Q: How to sideload a custom Swift app for personal use without a paid Apple Developer Program? A:

Short answer: pay Apple the yearly Developer fee.

The purpose of the 7-day limit is for those just getting into Apple/iOS development or need it for short term demos as described in Renew Free Provisioning Profile in Advance Apple. Should you want to create a custom personal/internal app which will expire with a longer period you'll need to spend the money to maintain a Apple Developer Account / Apple Enterprise Account.

Read through: https://developer.apple.com/help/account/membership/renewal/

As Apple is the one issuing the signing certificates that are attached to the app, your ability to run such software is at Apple's discretion.

Also see: Deploy iOS app on personal devices

Q: PyCharm Code Inspection warns about tkinter constants A:

This is a PyCharm-specific problem. ty, mypy, and Pyright correctly infer tk.LEFT to be of type Literal["left"] and accept your code accordingly. That's good, and it's made even more correct by the presence of Final hints throughout tkinter.constants in typeshed.1

Bryan Oakley's suggestion to use the underlying string literals ("left", etc.) will fix the immediate problem and shouldn't have any side effects. The constants themselves are defined to be those string literals internally, as are their typeshed hints; you don't lose any functionality by switching over.

My real recommendation, though—and I'm being completely serious—is to switch type checkers. Pycharm's is consistently below average; errors like this are par for the course. Installing an extension for another mainstream checker might be the most sustainable solution.

1 This "guarantees" that the names won't be reassigned, so they're always safe to be treated as literals.

Q: Herramienta/aplicación/ modelo (openai, perplexity, gemini, Claude....) A:

Please note that this is an English-only site. Could you formulate everything in English?

As to your question: I'm sure that no AI tools can make you an exceptional programming tutor. Moreover, one absolutely required condition for becoming a good tutor is being an exceptional software developer. Of course, I mean real software development, all on your own, without any AI assistance.

As to the AI, it certainly can be a good assistant, but hardly anything more. First of all, it can help you with the most boring parts of work. It can also help you to summarize the experience you gain. First and foremost: the AI can be only as smart as you are, not better.

Oh, and, by the way: if you think that an AI tool can make you a tutor, think also about this: if so, that tool can even better become a tutor without you, and tutor students without your assistence? What about such prospects?

Good luck!
